sections.title: Executive Summary
paragraphs: The aim of this document is to describe the web service Purchase Requisition in terms of "what is it" and "how to use it". It describes the webservice data-model, supported operation and related behavior and available interfaces.
Before going deeper with specific features of this webservice please ensure to review the document “J1P WS Development_Kit – Web Services Overview” which applies to all webservices
The structure of the current document is the following:
1. PR Import:

2. Request data format [PR Import]: describes the possible operations on import and describes the structure of the request. The request is composed of sections and every section is composed of fields to be filled. This paragraph specifies which fields are mandatory depending on the operation you want to perform and those that can be omitted.
3. Behavior [PR Import]: describes how the web service processes the data passed in input, in case of some particular processes.
4. Response Data Format [PR Import]: describes the structure of the web service response and contains the list of possible error codes.
5. PR Update:
6. Request data format [PR Update]: describes the structure of the update request.
7. Behavior [PR Update]: describes how the web service processes the data passed in input, in case of some particular processes
8. Response data format [PR Update]: describes the structure of the web service response and contains the list of possible error codes
9. PR Export:

10. Component filters [PR Export]: describes which sections of a purchase requisition can be exported. The use of a component filter increments the number of sections in the response to every purchase requisition exported.

11. Condition filters [PR Export]: describes which fields can be used to filter the purchase requisition to be extracted on specific conditions. So, the use of a condition filter allows to decrease the number of purchase requisition extracted.
12. Export data format [PR Export]: describes the structure of the response in terms of exported fields and sections.
13. Error codes [PR Export]: contains a list of possible error codes
14. PR Validate:

15. Request data format [PR Validate]: describes the structure of the validation request. The request is composed of sections and every section is composed of fields to be filled. This paragraph specifies which fields are mandatory and those that can be omitted.
16. Behavior [PR Validate]: describes how the web service processes the data passed in input
17. Response Data Format [PR Validate]: describes the structure of the web service response and contains the list of possible error codes

18. Data Types and UI Default Labels: describes the type of the fields and the corresponding label in English language in the platform with the aim to simplify the mapping between the fields visible in the platform and the fields used in the web service.

paragraphs: The web service call returns a code defining the result of the operation:
- 0: operation completed successfully
- 1: operation completed successfully with warnings as detailed in the returned message
- 2: operation not completed due to error as detailed in the returned message

sections.title: PR Export
paragraphs: Purchase Requisitions export method retrieves a list of information about JI Purchase Requisition matching optional filtering criteria.
This main Purchase Requisition setting information can be further enriched by specifically requesting additional information.
The list of returned requisition matching requested filter is always ordered by internal (JI) identifier in ascending order.

Export JI Purchase Requisitions Web Service method is paged. It needs a field “startAt” representing the index of the first record to be returned (according to last update date order). If not expressed or a not positive value is passed, the value 1 is assumed.

sections.title: Condition filters [PR Export]
paragraphs: Here are defined extraction condition filters, i.e. the rule to be used for data filtering.
A same condition filter can be expressed more than once. All specified filters are requested to be matched (they are all applied in AND clause).
Condition filters are also available server side as restrictive conditions. The filter conditions entered client side will be joined with the filter conditions configured server side.

It is possible to enable the component filters according to particular values of the condition filters server side. By this way, it is possible to configure different chains, everyone with different restrictive conditions and therefore with different subsets of component filters enabled.

For instance, based on the specific configuration set up for the single integration, will be possible to allow the webservice client to export only awarded auctions, even if this filter is not set by the integration client.

rows:
Date filtering accepts following operators:
EQUAL: auction last update date must be equal to provided value
NOTEQUAL: any auction whose last update date is different from provided value
GREATER_THAN: any auction whose last update date is equal or greater than provided value
LESS_THAN: any auction whose last update date is lower or than provided value

An RFx is a request for something:

Invitation to Negotiate (ITN)
Request for a Letter of Interest (RLI)
Valid RFx statuses are:
Draft – The RFx is being edited and has not yet been submitted for approval.
Pending – The RFx has been submitted for approval.
Approved – The RFx has been approved. Edits can no longer be made to the RFx.
Rejected – The RFx has been rejected during approval.
Released – The RFx is approved and has been posted on the external supplier portal.
Open – The RFx has been posted on the external supplier portal and is open for bids from suppliers.
Under Evaluation – The RFx is closed and is being evaluated for awarding.
Awarded – The RFx has been evaluated and awarded.
Closed Without Awarding – The RFx has been rejected during evaluation.
Canceled – The RFx has been canceled and will not be sent out for bid to suppliers.
Withdrawn – A Released or Open RFx has been canceled and will not be evaluated for awarding.
Stage Complete – For multi-stage events, the RFx has completed this stage (that is, a subsequent stage has been created).

sections.title: PR Validate
paragraphs: JI Purchase Requisition validate method allows to accept messages from a customer's ERP system to validate a requisition by entirely accepting or discarding it, or by signaling that some requisition line elements failed the validation while at least one of them succeeded.
It can also be used to update one or more line level, non-splittable custom fields.

paragraphs: Following table shows the structure of the validate request to submit.

When structure is defined at global header level, it can assume following value:

sections.title: Behavior [PR Validate]
paragraphs: When “validate” JIPurchaseRequisition method is called, system update the validation status that is shown by means of the “export” JIPurchaseRequisition method (see field “validationStatus” in chapter above).
To correctly manage such information, it is necessary to know the internal identifier of the requisition.
In case the “validate” JIPurchaseRequisition method is called to entirely validate object, this information is retrieved directly from the mandatory field “id” in provided data.
Instead, when calling method to validate at single line level, it is important to specify the value for the “requisitionId” field in “ValidateRequisitionLineDataList [PR Validate]” object structure.
If such field is not valorized, the validation status cannot be updated.

sections.title: Custom Field Update
paragraphs: At the line level, it is possible to return one or more custom fields in the response.
That enables to change the value of the custom field. The eProcurement solution can then move the PR to additional workflow steps, if needed.
When updating custom fields, it is important to consider that:
The PR must be in workflow
The custom field must be at the line level, and it must be non-splittable.
The custom field must already exist in the PR and in the eProcurement solution, and it must be active.
The custom field must have pre-populated values. Free text strings are not allowed.
For each type of custom field, the following values are allowed:
Check Box: Must be true or false
Date: Must be a date in the following format: yyyy-mm-dd.
List with predefined values, such as Dropdown List, Radio Button, or Multi-Select:
The new value must already exist in the eProcurement solution.
The new value must be active in the solution.
If a business unit is assigned to the PR, the new value must be available to that business unit
The value cannot be contained in the Codes section of the PR document.
